items.quote: If y ∝ x then y = m x
items.claim: If y varies directly as x then y = m x; and if y = m x then y ∝ x.
items.formula: $y \propto x \Rightarrow y = mx$ and $y = mx \Rightarrow y \propto x$

items.quote: If y ∝ x then y = 14 when x = 42, then find
items.stem: If $y \propto x$ then $y = 14$ when $x = 42$, then find first: the relation between x and y; second: find the value of y when $x = 60$.
solution: First: $\because y \propto x$, $\therefore y = mx$ (where m constant $\neq 0$)
Substitute for the values of x and y in the relation: $\therefore 14 = 42 \times m$, $\therefore m = \frac{14}{42} = \frac{1}{3}$, $\therefore$ the relation is: $y = \frac{1}{3}x$

items.quote: Connecting with Physics : If the relation between velocity (v)
items.stem: Connecting with Physics: If the relation between velocity (v) in (m/sec) and time t (sec) is $v = 9.8\,t$. First: determine the kind of variation between v and t. Second: A Find the values of v when t = 2 seconds, t = 4 seconds. B Find the value of t when v = 24.5 m/sec.
solution: First: $\because v = \text{constant} \times t$, i.e. $v \propto t$, i.e. v directly changes with t.
Second: A when t = 2 then $v = 9.8 \times 2 = 19.6$ m/s
B When V = 24.5 then $24.5 = 9.8 \times t$ $\therefore t = \frac{24.5}{9.8} = 2.5$ seconds.

parts.label: First
parts.stem: Determine the kind of variation between v and t.
parts.answer: v varies directly with t ($v \propto t$)

parts.label: Second A

parts.label: Second B
parts.stem: Find the value of t when v = 24.5 m/sec.

learning_objectives.label: Solve direct variation problems
learning_objectives.description: Determine the relation y = mx for a direct variation y ∝ x, find the constant m, and calculate unknown values of y or x.

learning_objectives.label: Solve inverse variation problems
learning_objectives.description: Determine the relation y = m/x for an inverse variation y ∝ 1/x, find the constant m, and calculate unknown values of y or x, including with a squared variable.

learning_objectives.label: Distinguish direct from inverse variation
learning_objectives.description: Determine from a table of x and y values whether the relation is a direct variation, an inverse variation or neither, giving the reason.
